bilello-us-debt-40t-five-month-rungs:
US federal debt passed $40 trillion on August 19.
It crossed $39 trillion in March of this year, and $38 trillion in October of last year.
Two consecutive trillion-dollar rungs took five months each.

@@REF@@The U.S. national debt now stands at $40 trillion (PBS NewsHour, 2026-08-19)|https://www.pbs.org/newshour/economy/the-u-s-national-debt-now-stands-at-40-trillion|https://d3i6fh83elv35t.cloudfront.net/static/2026/08/2026-08-19T211915Z_1898212623_RC2X1NAG108C_RTRMADP_3_USA-DEBT-1024x603.jpg

@@TIME@@July 2024|Debt passes $35 trillion|October 2025|Debt passes $38 trillion|March 2026|Debt passes $39 trillion|August 19, 2026|Debt passes $40 trillion|>Late winter to mid-summer 2027|Statutory ceiling of $41.1 trillion expected to be reached@@The last gap was five months and the one before it was five months too. The next rung runs into a wall.@@PBS NewsHour 2026-08-19 · US House Budget Committee release 2024-07-29

## A trillion every five months

A total on its own does not land.
Debt is felt first as the interest that goes out every month, not as the principal.
Buying a house works the same way: the monthly payment, not the loan size, sets how you live.

A government is no different.
The $40 trillion is not a sum to be repaid so much as a sum to be reborrowed at whatever rate prevails when each piece matures.
So what sets the budget is less the size of the pile than the rate attached to it.
With long-term yields rising, the same $40 trillion gets more expensive every year.
The more of it matures soon, the faster that repricing shows up.

@@CHK@@Total federal debt|$40 trillion|Annual interest cost|Over $1 trillion|Interest in the first 10 months of FY2026|Up 15% year over year@@What is growing faster than the pile is the interest on it. Interest is already the second-largest spending line after Social Security and larger than defense. The route by which debt squeezes a budget runs through this line, not through the headline total.@@Checked 2026-08-20 · Treasury debt total and interest figures as reported by NPR, 2026-08-19

## The line that crowds out the others

Interest payments now run above $1 trillion a year.
Lined up against other spending, they sit behind Social Security and ahead of defense.
Interest in the first ten months of fiscal 2026 was 15% higher than in the same stretch a year earlier.

Margaret Spellings, who leads the Bipartisan Policy Center, said the federal debt is already raising the cost of living and choking out other spending and investment.
Crowding out is not a metaphor here but a line in the budget. The money available in a year is fixed, and interest is not a line that politics sets. It is a line that contracts set.

@@REF@@National debt nears $40 trillion as warnings grow over economic toll (Spectrum News, 2026-08-18)|https://spectrumlocalnews.com/us/snplus/politics/2026/08/18/federal-deficit--40-trillion

## The two things that happened on August 19

On the same day the $40 trillion figure landed, the Treasury doubled its long-bond buybacks from $2 billion per operation to at least $4 billion.
A buyback is the government purchasing its own long-dated bonds back from the market to press long-term yields down.
The cash for it comes from newly issued debt.

That is where it splits.
If the new issuance is concentrated in short maturities, a larger share of the $40 trillion reprices within a year; if the long-dated share of issuance holds, the total grows while the maturity profile stays put.
In the first case long yields get pressed down but the budget becomes more sensitive to short rates, and in the second the buyback effect does not last.

There is also a wall on the next rung. The statutory ceiling of $41.1 trillion is expected to be reached somewhere between late winter and mid-summer of 2027.
If a trillion every five months holds, that date arrives sooner.
hanke-tomahawk-60-a-year-vs-1000-target-:
On August 18 the US Navy signed a $22.9 billion contract with Raytheon for Tomahawk cruise missiles.
It runs seven years, and the goal is to lift annual output above 1,000 missiles.
The United States currently builds about 60 Tomahawks a year.

@@REF@@Navy contract of $22.9 billion dramatically expands Tomahawk production (Stars and Stripes, 2026-08-18)|https://www.stripes.com/branches/navy/2026-08-18/navy-tomahawk-production-ramp-up-22589826.html|https://www.stripes.com/incoming/dxq970-190826tomahawkphoto06.jpg/alternates/LANDSCAPE_480/190826TOMAHAWKphoto06.JPG

A Tomahawk is a cruise missile fired from ships and submarines that flies more than a thousand kilometers.
It is what the Navy reaches for when it wants to hit something behind an air defense network without sending aircraft.

## 850 is not one month of firing

Hanke wrote that more than 850 were burned through in the first month of the war.
Checked against reporting outside the post, the period attached to that number is different.

@@REF@@US Tomahawks are being used in the Iran war faster than the stockpile is being refilled (CBS News, 2026-03-27)|https://www.cbsnews.com/news/u-s-tomahawks-iran-war-faster-than-stockpile-refilled/|https://assets2.cbsnewsstatic.com/hub/i/r/2026/03/27/65736de3-0d81-4d1f-a058-18051d870eaa/thumbnail/1200x630g2/8683146791bd2f231f7852520568eb46/gettyimages-2263711844.jpg

CBS reported in March that the figure of more than 850 was cumulative since the war began in June 2025.
It covered nine months, not one.
By August the total has passed 1,000, which is about a third of the roughly 3,000 missiles held before the war.

Stretching the period does not make the story lighter.
It moves the weight.
What matters is not how fast the stock was spent but how long it takes to put back.

## Between 60 and 1,000

@@BAR@@Current annual output|60 missiles|60|Target set by the contract|1,000 missiles|1000@@The multiple does not mean seventeen production lines. It means the flow of an item that takes 18 to 24 months from order to delivery has to be made that much thicker.@@Retrieved 2026-08-20. Stars and Stripes, 2026-08-18, for the current rate of 60 a year, the target above 1,000, and the 18-to-24-month lead time. CBS reported a rate of about 90 a year in March.

A Tomahawk costs roughly $2.2 million, and the newest Navy variants are reported to run above $4 million.
Dividing the award by seven years and 1,000 missiles a year gives about $3.3 million each.

So the contract is not buying only missiles.
Part of that money buys the lines, the suppliers, and forward orders for solid rocket motors and guidance sets.
Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao said production would be accelerated at unprecedented speed while current operations were still being supplied.

## Tomahawk is one of five

Raytheon signed five long-term agreements with the Pentagon, and Tomahawk is one of them.
The others cover the AMRAAM air-to-air missile, two versions of the SM-3 interceptor, and the SM-6.
Procurement is moving from buying missiles a year at a time toward committing to several years at once.

@@REF@@RTX's Raytheon partners with the Department of War on five landmark agreements to expand critical munition production (Barchart, 2026-08-18)|https://www.barchart.com/story/news/15929/rtx-s-raytheon-partners-with-department-of-war-on-five-landmark-agreements-to-expand-critical-munition-production

The place to check is fixed.
If deliveries in 2027 and 2028 climb into the hundreds per year, this contract bought capacity. If deliveries stay near today's rate, the money stays a promise on paper.
In a war that empties a magazine in weeks, the price is set less by what a weapon does than by how long it takes to build another one.

## Chinese customers paid the most

US export controls on advanced equipment make it hard for Chinese chip firms to secure leading-edge capacity at home.
So they have to print outside, and TSMC's lines are full.

@@REF@@Samsung raises foundry prices up to 15% as TSMC capacity fills (Seoul Economic Daily, 2026-08-19)|https://en.sedaily.com/international/2026/08/19/samsung-raises-foundry-prices-up-to-15-percent-as-tsmc|https://wimg.sedaily.com/news/cms/2026/08/19/news-p.v1.20260819.8025af188e3f4f8d9b6da46ca98bd117_P1.jpg

The Seoul Economic Daily lays out the same point: the controls leave Chinese firms leaning on foundries abroad.

Analysts in Seoul say that if these prices hold, the foundry unit could reach profitability earlier than expected.

What the late-October results will settle is not the size of the increase but the customer list.
If a TSMC customer such as Google signs on, this was a question of capacity rather than price. If the list looks the same, it was a price borrowed until the lines empty out.
meru-buyback-20b-offered-2b-taken-bill-f:
The US Treasury raised the size of its long-end buybacks from $2 billion to at least $4 billion per operation, and the reason sits in an operation held two days earlier.
In the August 18 operation for bonds maturing in 20 to 30 years, dealers offered roughly $20 billion of paper. The Treasury was permitted to take a tenth of that.

@@REF@@$20 billion offered, $2 billion taken: why Treasury doubled its buyback cap (FXStreet, 2026-08-19)|https://www.fxstreet.com/analysis/20-billion-offered-2-billion-taken-why-treasury-doubled-its-buyback-cap-202608191954|https://editorial.fxsstatic.com/images/i/Ondo-finance_Neutral_Medium.png

What it actually bought that day was $1 billion of a bond maturing in 2048 and $1 billion spread across two 2051s.
The cap went up at the exact spot where sellers outnumbered the buyer ten to one.

## A buyback is not a repayment

A buyback is the Treasury purchasing back old bonds that are already trading in the market.
The cash for it comes from selling new debt.
Nothing is retired on net. Only the maturity mix moves.

@@FLOW@@Issue bills|Sell new three-month paper to raise cash|Run the operation|Buy old long bonds back from dealers|Shrink the long end|Fewer long bonds circulate, so their price rises and their yield falls@@The path starts and ends at different maturities. Every long bond taken out is replaced by short paper that has to be borrowed again within months.

Long yields do fall along this path.
What remains open is where the cost of that lands.

## Buying 1.9% while issuing at 3.7%

Wolf Street took apart one of the securities bought in this operation.
It is a 30-year bond issued in February 2021, maturing in February 2051, carrying a coupon of 1.9%.
The Treasury bought it at 52.375 cents on the dollar.
That turned $334 million of face value into roughly $175 million of cash paid.

@@REF@@Bessent doubles the buybacks, swapping old cheap debt at a discount for new expensive debt (Wolf Street, 2026-08-19)|https://wolfstreet.com/2026/08/19/bessent-doubles-yellens-hocus-pocus-treasury-buybacks-swapping-old-cheap-debt-at-a-discount-for-new-expensive-debt/

Bought at half price, the face amount of the debt goes down.
But the old bond that disappeared cost $6.3 million a year to service, while the bills issued to fund the purchase cost about $7.0 million a year.
The debt shrank and the annual interest bill grew.

@@CHK@@Three-month bill rate|3.7%|Coupon on the bond bought|1.9%|30-year market yield|5.3%@@The coupon on the retired bond was fixed in the era of cheap money, while the short paper taking its place is priced at today's cost. The gap is narrower than the example in the original post (a 1.4% bond issued in 2020), but it points the same way. What a buyback moves is not the total interest bill but the placement of maturities.@@Retrieved 2026-08-20. FRED DTB3 and DGS30, values as of 2026-08-17. The coupon is CUSIP 912810SU3 as verified by Wolf Street.

The shortening of maturity comes with it.
Three-month paper matures four times a year, and each time it has to be borrowed again at whatever the rate is that day.
While rates sit where they are, that rollover passes quietly. Every rollover is also a repricing.

## What November 4 settles

The increase runs only from the September 9 operation through November 4.
Across seven operations in that window, the extra amount comes to $14 billion.
Against roughly $10 trillion of Treasuries outstanding in the 10-to-30-year sector, that addition is about a tenth of a percent.

So the force of this move is in the sentence rather than the sum.
It told anyone about to dump long bonds in a hurry that somebody is standing there to take them.

If the November 4 quarterly refunding keeps the larger size or raises it again, the interpretation the market bought in August was right.
If the size drops back to the old limit, this becomes a two-month piece of first aid.
What gets settled there is whether the long end is priced by the market or by the Treasury.
How long a price can be held up by changing maturities rather than paying down debt, and what it costs to let that price go, is what is riding on the answer.
serenity-marvell-google-warrant-120b-ves:

Exercised in full that is about $12.2 billion of stock, close to 7% of the company.
Marvell rose 12% on the day and traded above $230.

A warrant is a right a company issues that lets the holder buy newly issued shares at a set price.
The issuer parts with no cash, and the holder gains as the issuer grows.

## The right does not open by itself

The warrant splits in two.
In year one, 1,360,867 shares vest in equal quarterly instalments no matter what anyone buys.

The remaining 57.6 million shares work differently.
One tranche opens for every $500 million of custom-product revenue Google puts through Marvell, and there are 240 of those tranches.
The clock runs from Marvell's fiscal third quarter of 2027 to the end of fiscal 2033.

One extra floor takes a single building from four cleanrooms to six, and Samsung reckons capacity would rise by at least half again.

The Pyeongtaek campus has fixed boundaries, and its power, water and piping are already laid across that ground.
Buying new land means laying all of that again from scratch.

The number to take from that report is not the percentage but the reason behind it.

meru-hanwha-k9mh-mtc-six-prototypes-vs-5:
The US Army on August 18 picked Hanwha Defense USA to build prototypes of a wheeled self-propelled howitzer meant to replace the towed M777.
The award covers six vehicles for $100.3 million, and rises to eighteen vehicles if the Army exercises every option.

@@REF@@South Korea's highly mobile 155mm artillery system wins US Army howitzer contract (The War Zone, 2026-08-18)|https://www.twz.com/land/south-koreas-highly-mobile-155mm-artillery-system-wins-u-s-army-howitzer-contract|https://www.twz.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/army-picks-k9mh-155mm-howitzer-for-prototyping-effort.jpg?w=1200

American Rheinmetall, BAE Systems, General Dynamics Land Systems and Elbit Systems USA competed for the same work. Only Hanwha moved on to the prototype stage.

## What the units towing M777s are trying to fix

The M777 is a gun that a truck or a helicopter drags into position and sets down before it can fire.
Setting up takes time, and so does packing up and leaving.

On a battlefield covered by drones and counter-battery radar, the minutes a crew spends parked where it just fired are the minutes it is exposed.
Firing and immediately moving is what the Army calls shoot and scoot.
Hanwha says the K9MH takes under 30 seconds to emplace or displace.

The Army had been stretching the range of its existing M109 Paladin under a separate effort, ran into limits at the prototype stage, and shut that program down in 2024. After that it turned toward buying a design that already exists.

## The trade wheels make

Self-propelled artillery splits into tracked vehicles and wheeled ones.
Tracks spread the weight of the hull, so a tracked gun keeps moving through mud and up slopes, and it carries thicker armor.
The cost is weight and speed: moving one a long way usually means putting it on something else.

Wheels are the opposite trade.
A wheeled gun is lighter and faster, can drive hundreds of kilometers on its own, and fits inside a transport aircraft.
It pays for that with soft ground and thinner armor.

So the Army intends to leave tracked Paladins with its armored formations and give wheeled guns to the Stryker and infantry brigades that already move on wheels.
Hanwha's entry puts the automated turret of the in-service K9 onto an 8x8 wheeled chassis.

semianalysis-cerebras-cs4-same-wafer-dou:
Cerebras unveiled CS-4 on August 19, and there is no new chip in it.
The doubling comes from keeping the same 5nm wafer-scale engine, WSE-3, and pushing far more power into it to double the clock.
A rack now holds three wafers instead of two, and a single rack draws 125 to 135 kilowatts.

@@REF@@Cerebras intros faster WSE-3 Turbo processor and first rack-scale CS-4 system (ServeTheHome, 2026-08-19)|https://www.servethehome.com/cerebras-intros-faster-wse-3-turbo-processor-and-first-rack-scale-cs-4-system/|https://www.servethehome.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Cerebras-CS-4-Rack-Hero-Image-scaled.jpg

@@IMG@@https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/03/NVIDIA_GPU.jpg/960px-NVIDIA_GPU.jpg|A normal AI accelerator is a single chip about this size. Cerebras never cuts the chip out of the wafer; the whole wafer is the chip.|Mickael Courtiade · CC BY 2.0|https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:NVIDIA_GPU.jpg

A chipmaker usually cuts hundreds of rectangular dies out of one round 300mm wafer.
Cerebras does not cut. One wafer is one chip.

## Between 1,950x and 30x

@@BAR@@Cerebras on-chip bandwidth, one wafer|43,000TB/s|43000|NVIDIA Rubin HBM4 bandwidth, one GPU|22TB/s|22@@This is the number Cerebras leads with. Yet the speed advantage the same company claims is up to 30x against GPUs. When two multiples diverge this far, it means bandwidth is not what sets the speed.@@Checked 2026-08-19 · Cerebras CS-4 announcement materials (released 2026-08-18) · NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 product page, 22TB/s of HBM4 per GPU

ServeTheHome quotes 129.6 petabytes per second for a full rack, which is 43 multiplied by three wafers. The two figures agree.

## The 44-gigabyte ceiling

The memory etched into the wafer is SRAM.
It is far faster than the HBM stacked next to a conventional chip, and it holds far less.
One WSE-3 carries 44 gigabytes of it, and that number did not move from CS-3 to CS-4.
The number of storage cells is written into the silicon, so raising the clock does not add any.

Frontier model weights today run from hundreds of gigabytes into terabytes.
They do not fit in 44 gigabytes, so the model is sliced by layer and spread across several wafers.

A buyback is the Treasury purchasing old bonds that are already trading in the market.
The cash for those purchases comes from selling new bonds. The total stock of debt does not change; only its maturity mix does.

## $75.2 billion against $577 billion

@@BAR@@Buybacks scheduled Aug to Nov|$75.2bn|752|Net issuance, prior quarter|$577bn|5770@@A buyback does not shrink what the Treasury is printing. Over a comparable stretch, new borrowing runs more than seven times the amount being repurchased. So the number is not what moved yields.
El-Erian reads the market as buying the policy that could come next, not the operation itself.

## Naming the price before you buy

Yield curve control means a central bank or a government pinning a chosen maturity below a set level.
It fixes the price first and then promises to take whatever volume shows up at that price.

Yields do come down when this works.
What the authorities give up is control over quantity, because the sellers decide how much has to be absorbed to hold the line.
Fixing the price means handing over the volume, which is why leaving is far harder than entering.

YCC is not a free lunch, it invites collateral damage and unintended consequences, and the effects of this kind of financial engineering are short dated unless fundamental policy adjustments follow.

Steve Hanke wrote that half of Russia's refining capacity has been knocked out. That share depends entirely on what sits in the denominator.

## Crude piles up while diesel runs short

A refinery is where crude is boiled and separated into gasoline and diesel. When the plant stops, the crude does not vanish. It leaves the country as crude instead.

Prices therefore split in two directions.

More crude looks for buyers and its price is held down, while less refined fuel is made and its price rises. Put simply, the wheat is still there and the mill has burned; what gets expensive is flour, not wheat. On July 8 the US Gulf Coast diesel crack reached 64.58 dollars a barrel, close to a record, and European refining margins were above 60 dollars a barrel in the same stretch. The repair timeline follows from the same physical fact. What burns is the crude distillation unit or the catalytic cracker, equipment that takes a long time to build, and the spare parts and catalysts for it are hard to buy under Western sanctions.

Either way, treating crude and refined fuel as if they move together misreads this particular episode.

## Buying and retiring are not the same

A buyback is a company purchasing its own stock in the market. Shares bought that way can sit in the corporate treasury, and from there they can be resold later, handed to employees as compensation, or swapped for a stake in another company. A buyback on its own therefore does not shrink the share count.

Cancellation erases those shares from the register.

Retired shares never come back, so the number of shares outstanding falls permanently, and the same profit is divided among fewer of them. That is also why Korean policymakers treat the two steps differently. Lawmakers have been debating an amendment to the Commercial Act that would require repurchased shares to be cancelled within a set period, because treasury stock parked indefinitely can protect a controlling shareholder's voting power instead of enlarging what minority holders own. The fact that this announcement is written as a cancellation rather than a purchase is the part that matters.

meru-discount-rate-vs-thin-credit-spread:
The 30-year US Treasury yield has climbed to 5.3%, its highest level since 2007.
On the same day CoreWeave fell 8.3% and Fabrinet fell 10%,
while SK Hynix, SanDisk and Western Digital each dropped more than 5%.

@@REF@@Rising Yields, Oil Interrupt Rally, Hurting Chips (Charles Schwab, 2026-08-18)|https://www.schwab.com/learn/story/stock-market-update-open|https://www.schwab.com/sites/g/files/eyrktu1071/files/329122355_2x1.jpg

None of that means these companies will earn less money this year.
What shrank is the rate used to convert that money into today's value.

## Pushing 10 million won ten years out

The discount rate is the rate at which money you will receive later is marked down to what it is worth now.
Put simply, it is an interest rate turned around and run backwards.

Say you are due 10 million won a year from now.
At a 4% rate you only need to put 9.61 million won on deposit today to end up with 10 million,
so that future money is worth 9.61 million won today.
At 5% you need only 9.52 million won.
The same future sum just lost 90,000 won of present value.

Stretch the wait to ten years and the gap changes shape.
At 4% you need 6.76 million won today; at 5% you need 6.14 million.
The same one percentage point now costs 620,000 won, close to seven times the one-year figure.
Compounding does that: interest earns interest, and ten years of it piles up.

## Where banks and tech part ways

A bank that pays a steady dividend hands you money that behaves like one-year money.
The profits an AI company promises sit several years out.
So the same one percentage point moves the two share prices by very different amounts.

That is the first shock, and it arrives fast.
Nothing about the company's earnings changed. Only the price tag attached to those earnings did.

## When the spread is thin, the Treasury yield passes straight through

The second shock is slower.
Companies borrow at the Treasury yield plus a spread that reflects their own credit risk.
A wide spread absorbs part of a rise in Treasury yields. A thin one lets it through untouched.

That is the author's premise, so we went and looked the numbers up.

## When a cut and a runoff happen together

The answer the market is waiting for is a rate cut.
But what the policy rate moves directly is the short end.

The price of money you get back in 30 years is set by inflation over those 30 years and by how much paper the government prints in the meantime.
When the Fed shrinks its balance sheet, the long-dated bonds sitting in its vault flow back into the market.
The buyers stay the same while the supply grows, so the price falls, and a falling bond price is the same sentence as a rising yield.

@@CMP@@The common reading|If the Fed cuts, borrowing costs come down across the board, so the 30-year eventually follows.|Meru's reading|A cut lowers short rates while balance-sheet runoff pushes long bonds back onto the market. Do both and only the gap between short and long widens.

Readers split on how far the effect of the same cut travels, and what decides the split is not the size of the cut but the balance sheet.

## The resignation Warsh handed in during 2011

Only one tool pulls long yields down directly: quantitative easing, in which the Fed prints dollars and buys long-dated Treasuries.
The Treasury's own buyback swaps stale long bonds for freshly issued bills, so no new money enters the system.
Quantitative easing brings in money that did not exist and removes the long bonds outright. That single difference separates the two tools.

The problem is who holds that tool now. Kevin Warsh stepped down as a Fed governor in March 2011,
and the move is said to have followed his doubts about the second round of quantitative easing pushed by Ben Bernanke.
In 2014 he called quantitative easing a reverse Robin Hood policy that fed the market.
He was confirmed by the Senate 54 to 45 on May 13, 2026, and took the chair on May 22.

The piece reports that even before taking office Warsh sat on the side of cutting rates while continuing to shrink the balance sheet, and that the combination was contested inside the Fed.
This is the fuse Meru points at.
The cut is what Trump wants and the runoff is what Warsh wants, and doing both at once can send the 30-year the other way.

## The Senate vote scheduled for September

If the Fed will not move, where is the hand that can hold long yields down.
The remaining route is to issue fewer long bonds, and that requires someone to buy bills instead.

The CLARITY Act, waiting for another Senate vote in September, stands in that spot.
If the bill that sets the rules for crypto markets passes, the regulatory fog over dollar-pegged stablecoins lifts,
and issuers hold most of their reserves in short-term US Treasuries.
Fed Governor Stephen Miran said in a November 2025 speech that the interquartile range of private estimates compiled by Fed staff puts stablecoin uptake at $1 trillion to $3 trillion by the end of the decade.

If that much demand for bills appears, the Treasury can issue more short and less long, holding long yields down by going around them.
If the Senate reaches 60 votes in September, one more hand joins the effort, and if it falls short again what is left is the slow road of waiting for inflation to come down on its own.
So to read the direction of the 30-year now, watching the Fed chair's convictions and the Senate's vote count works faster than watching what else the Treasury secretary pulls out.

This is not a loan.
SB Energy, a SoftBank company, builds and owns the land, the generation and the buildings.
Nvidia's role is to stand behind that company when it borrows from lenders.

A guarantee lowers the risk the lender carries, and cheaper debt follows.
Think of a parent co-signing a child's mortgage.
The parent does not buy the house; the parent makes the bank lend at a lower rate.

## Three cuts in three weeks

## Between 4.25 and 8

The scope Jensen Huang wrote out himself on LinkedIn is narrow.
The support covers roughly four gigawatts over a 20-year term, and it runs to defined portions of lease and power payments plus a specified residual-value commitment.
He also wrote what it is not: not the full cost of the site, and not all of the tenant's obligations.

Eight gigawatts is the compute OpenAI intends to lease.
What has been backed today is the 4.25 gigawatts of the first phase, and the remaining 3.75 gigawatts sits as an option Nvidia may or may not take.

## Why land and power of all things

The campus rises on the decommissioned Portsmouth gaseous diffusion plant, a Department of Energy site in Pike County that once enriched uranium for naval reactors.

The electricity is being built from scratch.
Ten gigawatts of new generation is planned, 9.2 gigawatts of it natural gas, and SB Energy and SoftBank are putting at least $4.2 billion more into regional grid infrastructure through AEP Ohio.

That is the price of making a place to plug the chips in, before anyone buys a chip.

## From 2028, when Pike County switches on

Huang wrote that the guarantee becomes effective in phases.
As each data center is placed in service between 2028 and 2030 the matching slice of the guarantee comes alive, and as OpenAI makes lease payments Nvidia's remaining exposure declines.

So the weight of this promise is set in 2028, not today.
If OpenAI keeps generating the cash to pay rent, the guarantee stays paper.
If it does not, Nvidia inherits somebody else's building and somebody else's power bill.
Rather than argue about whether the structure is circular financing, watch when Nvidia puts its name on the remaining 3.75 gigawatts.
Filling that slot means it has taken the full eight gigawatts onto its own risk; leaving it empty means 4.25 gigawatts is the limit Nvidia chose.

Against a defense budget then running near $700 billion, the share ends below the decimal point.

The real cost-sharing sits somewhere else.
South Korea's contribution to stationing US forces is 1.5192 trillion won for 2026, 8.3% above the 1.4028 trillion won paid in 2025.

Wartime operational control is the authority to command South Korean forces in a war, and it currently rests with the commander of the combined forces.
One condition for handing that authority to South Korea is a full operational capability verification confirming that its military can run combined operations.

That verification happens only inside a joint exercise.
Yet the two sides had already agreed that this year's Ulchi Freedom Shield would run without South Korea in the lead, with verification targeted for completion by the November alliance meeting.
An order to shrink the exercise lands on top of that schedule.

## The August 18 open is the first answer

Korean markets were shut on August 17 for a substitute Liberation Day holiday, so there is no price yet for this announcement.
On August 14, the last session before it, the KOSPI had risen for five straight days and was approaching 7,000.

The test is not the name of the drill but November.
If the alliance meeting delivers both a completed capability verification and a target year for the command transfer, this order was a negotiating line.
If the verification slips to a later date, the reduction reached the procedure itself, and cost-sharing talks and troop numbers come onto the same page.
That is also where Korean defense shares split on this news. A thinner alliance reads as a bigger domestic procurement budget, but an actual troop cut puts regional risk back into the price.
